- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% for 30-day horizons.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits strong mean-reversion bias — forecasts drift toward historical mean too aggressively; apply a 0.5–1.0% upward adjustment to prevent undershoot.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect; dampen forecast slope by 15–20% in 3–5 day windows post-spike.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in the first 5–7 days of the 30-day horizon; apply a 1–3% downward bias to early days if recent history shows downward momentum.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65), model tends to ignore it; adjust forecast to align with 20-day moving average of true values for 30-day horizon.
